note: Maps requirements (§2.2) and acceptance tests (§18) to test tags and the phase that must cover them. status 'covered' means every tag must appear in a passing test in reports/vitest-junit.xml; 'partial' is the same check plus a note on what remains; 'planned' has no tests yet.

entries.note: 95 cross-language vectors; scripts/check-contracts.mjs reruns the Python implementation.
Markdown projection for every family, and no-JavaScript reading of every example (chromium-nojs).
Frontmatter docId schema, duplicate-ID rejection, ID stability under moves, a fork (copy) that gets a new docId and keeps target IDs, and retire (deletion) that resolves deleted.
Every target kind across the examples (32 kinds, including figure) is selected in reference mode and resolves exact through the CLI.
Edges and nodes open labelled details with evidence from the SVG and from the relationship list (browser journeys).
Definition tooltip on hover/focus and tap-to-open. Real touch-device review is a human gate.
Narrow and no-JS views carry the same target and relationship sets as the model for every example, including order, branch, and exclusivity data.

Committed capture ignores a dirty working tree; working-tree captures are labelled and compared as working-tree matches; example and link-only sources; unavailable origins and hostile repositories (replace refs, partial clones, gitfiles, alternates) fail closed.
scripts/check-offline.mjs proves network isolation under unshare -rn, then runs init, check, build, both exports, and serve over loopback.
User and repository scopes; two repositories resolve one user installation through the shim; trust gate for repository toolchains; strict release verification.

Reproducible release archive, strict ustar reader, install --from-release against local HTTPS servers with a test CA, site export with relative URLs, and the browser journeys against a /visser-demo/ subpath export on a static server. Real GitHub hosts are not tested (no network).

Variables, functions, if/partial, raw HTML, and unknown tags are rejected before transform. An untrusted extension whose build entry writes a sentinel never runs (build, export, check, fallback build, inspect).
Packets resolve by doc ID and target ID; renamed folders, forged hints, and the browser-copied packet resolve through the CLI.
Stale packets refuse guarded writes; refresh is required; concurrent-writer check before rename (T20).
Desktop HTML, narrow view, no-JS view, and the Markdown projection derive the same target and relationship tuples.

Extensions expose source-visible part targets, a text fallback, and schema-checked attributes; output passes the core SVG allowlist. Parts have no relationship tuples in v1, and there is no browser test of an extension page.

format.md snippets and catalogue templates compile; guides match the tag rules; check --review flags every bad editorial fixture and no good one. The human comprehension trial is prepared but not run (docs/validation/comprehension-trial.md), so this stays partial.
Manifest-only server: GET/HEAD only, Host allowlist, no source or guessed paths, encoded traversal rejected.
Source revision, build ID, canonical JSON, and cross-language vectors.
ids assign, guarded replace, retire, and capture keep every other target ID and body hash; frontmatter edits keep every other key.
Public export refuses private documents, unlisted source repositories, and development builds; Mermaid comments are removed from pages and document.md.

Section 2.3 size and count gates (reader.js, reader.css, per-document JS, release browser assets, skill size, graph caps) on a 5,000-word reference fixture, and gzip in serve. Timing is reported only, in docs/validation/budgets.md: the initial usable page is 635.5 ms with gzip (target 2 s).
Renamed heading keeps its ID; old packet is stale.
Inserting a paragraph above a target keeps its ID and shifts only its span.
A moved edge resolves stale with targetBodyUnchanged=true, from a browser-copied packet.
Identical paragraphs get independent IDs and spans, and resolve independently by ID, never by quote.
Duplicate IDs fail with E_ID_DUPLICATE (fixtures/negative/E_ID_DUPLICATE). Resolver-level rejection is Phase 1.
fork gives a new doc ID; original packets do not address the fork.
retire and merge give deleted with an advisory replacement only.
A renamed document folder resolves by doc ID.
The packet keeps the viewed revision; resolve surfaces staleness after the source changes.
Packet agreement checks and resolver-level invalid for a wrong body at the current revision.
A forged sourceHint cannot choose a file.
One canonical element per target; instances carry data-vs-target without duplicate HTML IDs.
A cross-block selection is refused explicitly, never silently truncated.
Same source with a different toolkit gives a different build ID.
A guarded replace changes only the target and its ancestors.
Retiring a nested edge: the edge resolves deleted and its container stale.
Retire with a live referrer is refused with E_REF_BROKEN and lists the referrers.
Dropping a nested ID is rejected with E_ID_RETENTION.
Refresh after a body change needs --acknowledge-body-change.
An external write before rename gives E_WRITE_CONFLICT.
